script55_side_by_side.script55_supported_column_note: µ_nominal·F on the 18 mm PEEK gap propped where the bore begins — the §2 «supported» idealisation; script 55 measures it against these caps itself (clearance_regime.supported_column_vs_equilibrium)
script55_side_by_side.coaxial_cap_bound: LOWER end — rigid wall; see drag_coaxial[].coaxial_cap_bound

summary: Coaxial channel: under pogo drag the rod meets the wall only at the pad plane, where the tube ends flush; against a RIGID wall the root stress is µ-invariant — 3.40 MPa on the shipped geometry (the whole Zone-1 lock shank inserted, HW.26 G1), 2.73 MPa at the lock window's shallow end (zero-interference play, bonded member) — and that figure is the LOWER end of the root stress: the polymer wall on the Ti bore's edge yields by R/k, and the upper end (the Ti-bore stop, or the free cantilever where the drag cannot reach the bore) is 23.8 MPa on the shipped geometry and 19.1 MPa at the shallow end at the worst swept µ; where in that bracket the root sits is set by the contact compliance, measured nowhere. Script 55's 18 mm supported column prices that section at 55.00 MPa nominal — compare it with the rigid-wall end per geometry above. Channel off the root axis: past the play the mouth becomes a contact station and the STATIC root bending grows at a secant 0.64 MPa/µm on the shipped geometry and 0.42 MPa/µm at the shallow end. Reversing drag on a static offset, amplitude over the swept offsets — shipped — the whole lock shank (HW.26 G1): up to 4.15 MPa against its cap 3.40 (ABOVE it); lock window, shallow end: up to 3.76 MPa against its cap 2.73 (ABOVE it). A pogo contact off the rod axis by the rod radius, with the worst drag, gives up to 5.88 MPa on the shipped geometry and 5.22 MPa at the shallow end. The tilt price depends on the PIVOT (root · mouth · pad plane) far more than on the angle. Peak moment: the root is the peak-moment section in every drag, offset and reversing-drag row; it leaves the root only in tilt shipped — the whole lock shank (HW.26 G1) mouth/9.0 mrad, tilt lock window, shallow end mouth/9.0 mrad, pad_moment shipped — the whole lock shank (HW.26 G1) e +0.5 mm, pad_moment lock window, shallow end e +0.5 mm. MEASURED: contact stations and root stress for swept geometry, play, offset, tilt and pad moment. NOT computed: what the stack delivers, contact pressure, a varying offset's amplitude, weld compliance. No verdict is taken here.

not_modelled.wall: rigid and frictionless — no liner compliance, no contact pressure, no axial traction. The SIGN of that omission differs by regime: under coaxial DRAG the rigid-wall root stress is the LOWER end — a compliant polymer wall lets the exit yield by R/k and raises the root moment by 3EI·(R/k)/L², up to the Ti-bore stop or the free cantilever (drag_coaxial[].by_mu[].sigma_root_MPa_upper_end); past the play under an OFFSET the mouth corner would load the PEEK tube beyond its compressive strength at the larger offsets, so offset stresses are UPPER bounds. The contact compliance that places either is measured nowhere
not_modelled.clamp: perfect — weld and printed-anode compliance lower every stress
not_modelled.swept_not_measured: insertion, play, offset, tilt and pad eccentricity
not_modelled.mean_stress: a static offset is a mean stress; no Goodman-type correction; the amplitude of a varying offset needs relative Zone-1<->Zone-3 motion, measured nowhere
not_modelled.drag_contact_edge: the drag contact is the flush tube end at the pad-plane exit — ring on ring, the edge form the ≥ 1.0 mm protrusion avoids at the mouth — and no exit radius is specified anywhere; the wall reaction there is the drag minus the touchdown force on every cycle
not_modelled.other: small deflection, no thermal term, no liner creep, no P-δ from the axial pogo force
